lead.tldr: HYPE funds attract $72M, 59% rise, capital shifting from BTC/ETH ETFs to alt‑coin ETFs • Nasdaq PHLX's conditional approval of cash‑settled Bitcoin index options lowers institutional hedging barriers • NEAR's cross‑chain Intents generate $19B volume, fueling 15% token rally ahead of dynamic resharding upgrade • Ethereum Foundation plans to trim ETH holdings, reduce sales, emphasizing CROPS principles, reducing founder influence • Prometheum's broker‑dealer distribution platform could unlock tokenized securities mainstream, pending regulatory clarity

intro: Dear Founders, Investors, and Friends, HYPE ETFs are pulling billions from Bitcoin funds while Nasdaq readies cash‑settled Bitcoin options, and NEAR’s cross‑chain activity drives a fresh price surge. Meanwhile, Hyperliquid expands into tokenized assets as regulators clamp down on prediction markets.

top_signals.title: HYPE funds attract millions as investors dump bitcoin and ether ETFs
top_signals.summary: Institutional investors have withdrawn more than $1 billion from Bitcoin ETFs and $215 million from Ether funds, reallocating capital toward newer alt‑coin products such as HYPE, XRP and SOL ETFs. The HYPE token, launched by Bitwise and 21Shares, has attracted roughly $72 million of inflows and posted a 59 percent price gain this month. The shift reflects growing demand for higher‑yield, niche crypto exposure beyond the flagship Bitcoin and Ether offerings. At the same time, Hyperliquid’s trading platform is reporting rising fee revenue and has added a USDC integration, further supporting the alt‑coin momentum.

top_signals.title: Bitcoin options are coming to Nasdaq. Here's what it means for you
top_signals.summary: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission has given conditional approval for Nasdaq PHLX to list cash‑settled, European‑style Bitcoin index options under the ticker QBTC. The product still requires CFTC sign‑off before it can be launched. With a contract size of one Bitcoin and settlement in U.S. dollars, the offering is designed to reduce entry barriers for institutional and retail investors who want to hedge or trade Bitcoin volatility on the same exchange used for equities.

top_signals.title: NEAR price rally gains momentum as cross-chain product activity fuels further 15% jump
top_signals.summary: NEAR Protocol’s native token rose 15 percent to $2.8, continuing a month‑long rally that has almost doubled its price. The price gain is linked to heightened usage of NEAR Intents, the platform’s cross‑chain infrastructure. NEAR Intents has processed more than $19 billion in transaction volume and generated $32 million in fees. Market participants are also pricing in a forthcoming June upgrade that will introduce dynamic resharding to improve scalability.

top_signals.title: Vitalik Buterin breaks silence about Ethereum Foundation amid community frustration
top_signals.summary: Vitalik Buterin addressed community frustration by outlining a new strategic direction for the Ethereum Foundation. He said the Foundation will deliberately reduce its ETH holdings and scale back token sales. The organization will prioritize the CROPS principles: censorship resistance, capture resistance, openness, privacy and security. Buterin also noted his personal influence on the board will lessen as the Foundation expands, positioning it as one node among many in the broader ecosystem.

top_signals.title: Hyperliquid (HYPE) is emerging as a challenger to traditional exchanges and prediction markets, says FalconX
top_signals.summary: Hyperliquid (HYPE) is expanding its offering beyond crypto perpetual futures to include pre‑IPO contracts, prediction markets, and tokenized real‑world assets. This diversification positions the platform as a direct competitor to legacy exchanges such as CME and ICE. FalconX reports strong inflows into the newly launched HIP‑3 and HIP‑4 markets and notes a USDC partnership with Coinbase and Circle that could accelerate platform growth.

top_signals.title: Indonesia blocks Polymarket, calling prediction market online gambling in disguise
top_signals.summary: Indonesia's Ministry of Communication and Digital Affairs has blocked access to Polymarket, a crypto‑based prediction market platform. The ministry classified the platform as illegal online gambling. The action follows similar bans in India and reflects a growing regulatory trend across Asia targeting prediction‑market services that enable wagering on real‑world events. Institutional investors should note the heightened legal risk for crypto‑enabled betting platforms in the region.

top_signals.title: Prometheum says tokenized securities need Wall Street distribution to scale
top_signals.summary: Prometheum introduced an infrastructure enabling SEC‑registered broker‑dealers and registered investment advisers to sell tokenized securities via existing brokerage platforms. The company says that widespread Wall Street distribution channels, rather than just issuance, are essential for scaling blockchain‑based securities. This approach could allow institutional investors to access digital assets within familiar regulatory and compliance frameworks.

top_signals.title: What next as bitcoin (BTC) and Asian equities cheer oil price slide?
top_signals.summary: Bitcoin remained above $77,000, trading just above its 50‑day moving average. The price level was supported by a more than 5% decline in oil prices following reports of a possible reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. The drop in oil lifted Asian equity markets, indicating broader risk‑on sentiment. However, spot Bitcoin ETF investors withdrew more than $2 billion over the past two weeks, prompting analysts to remain cautious about near‑term demand.
